elements.element: Customer owns each Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 states that Customer exclusively owns each Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause addresses defined Deliverables only. It does not mention work product or establish that all work product is included within Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor presently assigns to Customer all rights in each Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Vendor 'hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to the Deliverables.'

elements.element: Vendor presently assigns to Customer all rights in all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The assignment covers Deliverables only and does not expressly cover work product outside that category.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No operative pre-existing-IP reservation appears in the rendered clause. The margin reference to Section 14.3 is non-operative, and the unqualified Deliverable assignment could encompass Vendor IP included in a Deliverable.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The clause grants a licence only where a Deliverable is not assignable. It does not reserve and license Vendor IP embedded in an otherwise assignable Deliverable.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Although the non-assignability backstop licence is perpetual, there is no licence specifically covering embedded Vendor IP to which this duration applies.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Although the non-assignability backstop licence is irrevocable, there is no licence specifically covering embedded Vendor IP to which this protection applies.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Although the non-assignability backstop licence is royalty-free, there is no licence specifically covering embedded Vendor IP to which this economic term applies.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 confirms Customer's ownership of all Customer Data and gives Vendor only a limited processing right for specified service purposes.

elements.element: The clause does not provide for joint ownership.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 provides for Customer's exclusive ownership of Deliverables, and no operative language creates joint ownership.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no reservation of ownership for Vendor's generic tools; the broad assignment may instead transfer rights in tools included in a Deliverable.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not state that Vendor retains ownership of its know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence covering every Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The express licence applies only '[t]o the extent any Deliverable is not assignable.' There is no unconditional licence covering every Deliverable, and the triggering condition is not demonstrably applicable to all Deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The express non-assignability backstop licence is stated to be perpetual; the separate failure to cover every Deliverable is assessed in the licence-coverage element.

elements.element: The licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The express non-assignability backstop licence is stated to be irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The express non-assignability backstop licence is stated to be worldwide.

elements.element: The licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The express non-assignability backstop licence is stated to be royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The express licence permits Customer to use the applicable Deliverable for any business purpose.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The express licence permits Customer to modify the applicable Deliverable for any business purpose.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The express licence is sublicensable and applies for any business purpose.

result.reason: The redline clearly gives Customer ownership and a present assignment of Deliverables, preserves Customer Data ownership, and includes a robust non-assignability licence. It nevertheless fails the preferred position because it omits work product, contains no pre-existing Vendor IP carveout, and does not license embedded Vendor IP. It fails the fallback because Vendor ownership of generic tools and know-how is not preserved and the express licence covers only non-assignable Deliverables. The changes are not minimal because they add several rights beyond either stated position while omitting required protections, including Affiliate rights, transferability, reproduction, and derivative-work rights. The omission of the Vendor-IP reservation also undermines the intended ownership allocation.
